obernants.domain: Finite byte slices and ordinary terminating executions with successful allocation.
obernants.assumptions: Rust byte-slice semantics and successful allocation; transformation premises as stated.
obernants.observation_scope: One public call or explicitly scoped internal state.
obernants.operator: Exclude omitted, repeated or out-of-range offsets, the empty suffix n, or adjacent offsets whose suffixes are in descending order. Input bytes remain unchanged.
obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived relation; bounded checks are not universal proofs.

obernants.operator: For a fixed permutation A of 0..n, compatible byte texts are precisely length-n texts whose adjacent suffixes T[A[j]..] are strictly lexicographically increasing. Several texts satisfy these constraints; A alone does not recover bytes.

obernants.operator: Observe rank ordering and equality, not the initial literal numeric byte ranks. At width k, equal ranks mean equal length-k truncated suffix prefixes and rank order matches their lexicographic order. Any byte text with the same ordered prefix equivalence classes is compatible with this rank observation.
obernants.approximation_semantics: Source-derived relation; bounded checks are not universal proofs.

obernants.operator: Each round doubles represented prefix length unless all n ranks are unique and returns. Width>=n distinguishes suffix lengths even for constant bytes. checked_add handles absent tails; saturating doubling cannot prevent termination for valid byte slices.
